Passing the CKA: My Battle-Tested Playbook (18 Months Later) Hey there! So, I passed the CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator) exam about 18 months ago, and I’ve been meaning to write this down ever since. Better late than never, right?
Why This Guide? Look, there are tons of CKA guides out there. Most of them are… well, let’s just say they’re not exactly what I needed when I was studying. I wanted something practical, something that tells you what actually works, not just theory.
My Approach I’m not gonna lie, I spent way more time than I should have preparing. But hey, it worked! Here’s what I did:
Practice, practice, practice - I set up a local cluster and broke things on purpose Learn the shortcuts - kubectl has some amazing aliases and shortcuts Know your docs - The official Kubernetes docs are your best friend during the exam Key Commands That Saved Me Here are some commands that I used constantly:
# Quick pod logs kubectl logs -f <pod-name> # Get all resources in a namespace kubectl get all -n <namespace> # Quick port forward kubectl port-forward <pod-name> <local-port>:<pod-port> Final Thoughts The exam is challenging, but it’s totally doable if you prepare properly. Focus on hands-on practice, know your kubectl commands, and don’t panic if something doesn’t work immediately.
Good luck!

Who Am I? Hey there! I’m a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) based in New York Paris, deeply passionate about Kubernetes, DevOps, and Cloud Computing.
But not only! I also love science in general, and I’m curious about absolutely everything (yes, it’s time consuming). As you can see below, I even did a CRISPR 101 bootcamp.
My Journey I started my career as a Linux enthusiast, tinkering with servers, optimizing infrastructure, and automating everything I could. Over time, I delved into Kubernetes, Terraform, and cloud platforms like AWS, refining my skills in container orchestration, automation, and infrastructure as code.
Today, I specialize in Kubernetes, networking, and Low level stuff, aiming to contribute to open-source projects.
Why This Blog? I created KubeOrNotToBe to share insights, best practices, and real-world experiences from the trenches. Whether it’s debugging Kubernetes issues, CI/CD pipelines, or exploring new DevOps tools, you’ll find practical content here.
And most importantly: Sharing is caring! If you see any possible improvements, don’t hesitate! I’m in constant learning mode and open to any advice! It also goes both ways if you need any advice or anything else, feel free to ask!
Some topics I’d love to cover:
Kubernetes deep dives (controllers, operators, networking, and security) Cloud-native tooling (Helm, Terraform, Ansible) SRE methodologies (incident management, observability, and chaos engineering) DevOps automation (GitOps, CI/CD, and IaC) Hacking and security (CKA/CKS preparation, securing clusters, pentesting cloud environments) Let’s Connect! If you’re passionate about Kubernetes, DevOps, or simply sciences in general, let’s chat!
GitHub: @0xbochi LinkedIn: BOSCH luckas (French) Twitter/X: @0xbochi Misc: LinkTree Stay tuned for more content, and happy learning! 🛠️🚀
